Synapse R Client Overview

2026-10-02

synapser.Rmd

Overview

The synapser package provides an interface to Synapse, a collaborative workspace for reproducible data intensive research projects, providing support for:

  • integrated presentation of data, code and text
  • fine grained access control
  • provenance tracking

The synapser package lets you communicate with the Synapse platform to create collaborative data analysis projects and access data using the R programming language. Other Synapse clients exist for Python, Java, and the web browser.

If you’re just getting started with synapser, have a look at the Getting Started guides: Installation, Authentication, and Configuration.

Good example projects are:

  • TCGA Pan-cancer (syn300013)
  • Development of a Prognostic Model for Breast Cancer Survival in an Open Challenge Environment (syn1721874)
  • Demo projects (syn1899339)

This page gives a short tour of what you can do with synapser. Each section links to a tutorial that covers the topic in depth.

Installation

Install synapser from the Synapse R repository (RAN):

install.packages("synapser", repos = c("http://ran.synapse.org", "https://cloud.r-project.org"))

Alternatively, edit your ~/.Rprofile and configure your default repositories:

options(repos = c("http://ran.synapse.org", "https://cloud.r-project.org"))

after which you may run install.packages without specifying the repositories:

install.packages("synapser")

synapser sets up the Synapse Python client it needs the first time it is loaded, so you don’t need to install Python yourself. For detailed installation instructions, including installing from GitHub, see the Installation vignette. For troubleshooting, see the Troubleshooting guide.

Connecting to Synapse

To use Synapse, you’ll need to register for an account. The Synapse website can authenticate using a Google account. If you authenticate using a Google account, you’ll need to create a personal access token to log in to Synapse through the programmatic clients. See the Authentication vignette for more information.

Once that’s done, you’ll be able to load the library and login:

library(synapser)
synLogin()

For more ways to manage your Synapse credentials, please see the Authentication vignette, and the native reference documentation:

?synLogin
?synLogout

Accessing Data

Synapse identifiers start with syn, followed by numbers (for example, syn123). Upload a local file with synStore(), and download a file with synGet():

file = File(path = "/path/to/data.csv", parent_id = "syn123") |> synStore()

downloaded_file = synGet(
  file$id,
  file_options = FileOptions(download_location = "/path/to/downloads/")
)
downloaded_file$path

By default, files are downloaded to the Synapse cache. See Data Upload, Download, and Delete and Files for more, including versioning. To move many files at once, see Uploading data in bulk, Downloading data in bulk, and Downloading data by Synapse ID.

Organizing Data in a Project

Projects and folders are containers that organize your data:

project = Project(name = "My uniquely named project") |> synStore()
folder = Folder(name = "raw_data", parent_id = project$id) |> synStore()

To list what a project or folder contains without downloading anything, sync its metadata:

project = project |> synSyncFromSynapse(download_file = FALSE, recursive = FALSE)
for (child in project$folders) {
  print(child$name)
}

See Projects, Folders, and Structuring Your Synapse Project.

Annotating Synapse Entities

Annotations are key-value metadata that make your data searchable. Set them with synSetProperties() and save them with synStore():

file = synGet(file$id, file_options = FileOptions(download_file = FALSE)) |>
  synSetProperties(annotations = list(assay = "RNA-seq", fileType = "csv")) |>
  synStore()
file$annotations

See Add, Update and Remove Annotations and Properties and annotations.

Provenance

Synapse’s provenance tools record what was used, and what was executed, to create a file. Attach an Activity to an entity and store it:

file = synGet(file$id, file_options = FileOptions(download_file = FALSE)) |>
  synSetProperties(
    activity = Activity(
      name = "clustering",
      description = "whizzy clustering",
      used = list(UsedEntity(target_id = "syn1234")),
      executed = list(UsedURL(name = "analysis code", url = "https://github.com/my-org/my-analysis"))
    )
  ) |>
  synStore()

See Activity/Provenance and the Activity reference documentation (?Activity).

Tables

Synapse Tables store tabular data that can be queried using a SQL-like query language. See Tables, Virtual Tables, and Dataset Collection.

Wikis

Wiki pages let you describe your project and its data in Markdown:

wiki_page = WikiPage(
  owner_id = project$id,
  title = "My Wiki Page",
  markdown = "# My Wiki Page\n\nThis is a wiki page."
) |> synStore()

See Wikis.

Evaluations

An Evaluation is a queue that accepts and scores submissions, for example in a computational challenge. Submit an entity to an evaluation queue:

submission = Submission(
  entity_id = file$id,
  evaluation_id = "9999999",
  name = "My Submission"
) |> synStore()

See Evaluations and Submissions, SubmissionStatuses, SubmissionBundles.

Sharing Access to Content

By default, data you upload is private to you. Share it by setting permissions for a user, a team, or everyone, for example to give the public read access:

project |> synSetPermissions(principal_id = 273949L, access_type = list("READ"))

See Sharing Settings (ACL Management) and Access Control.

File Views

A file view can be defined by its scope. It allows querying for files within the scope using a SQL-like syntax. Please visit the EntityView vignette for more information.

Accessing the API Directly

These methods enable access to the Synapse REST(ish) API taking care of details like endpoints and authentication. See the REST API documentation.

?synRestGet
?synRestPost
?synRestPut
?synRestDelete

Synapse Utilities

Utilities that used to live in the separate synapserutils package are now available directly in synapser:

  • Copy files, folders, and projects with synCopy().
  • Upload data to Synapse in bulk with synSyncToSynapse() (see Uploading data in bulk).
  • Download data from Synapse in bulk with synSyncFromSynapse() (see Downloading data in bulk).

More information

For more information see the Synapse User Guide.
